name: ML Interviews
strandNote: Optional on every quant track. For machine learning researcher interviews at funds and AI labs.
description: Answer deep learning theory questions aloud, write the standard pieces from scratch against the clock, and work a deep learning case at a fund.

requires.why: Answers backpropagation questions by hand, built on the scalar MLP and gradient check of backprop level 3.
Answers optimiser, initialisation, normalisation and regularisation questions from nn-train levels 1 to 3.
Reuses the spoken answer form and the bias-variance answer from research-int level 2.
Writes masked multi-head attention, taught in sequence level 3.
Writes a layer's backward pass in NumPy, as in the array autograd of backprop level 4.
Writes k-means from scratch; the algorithm and its several starts come from that lesson.
Uses the drill stopwatch and the two-in-sixty session plan from coding-int level 4.

levels.name: A deep learning case at a fund

requires.why: Works the case in the order of research-int level 3: frame, baseline, model, present.
Compares a network with the gradient boosting and walk-forward tree study of ensembles level 3.
Splits returns by time, with walking forward and purging from validation level 2.
Compares models across seeds with the experiment habits of nn-train level 4.

lessonObjectives.l1-backprop-on-a-whiteboard: Derive the gradients of a two-layer network by hand and explain each step aloud.
lessonObjectives.l2-why-adam: Explain Adam's two moving averages and its bias correction, and when SGD with momentum is preferred.
lessonObjectives.l3-double-descent: Explain why test error peaks where parameters equal data points and falls again past it.
lessonObjectives.l4-deep-learning-quickfire: Answer short questions on initialisation, normalisation, dropout, attention scaling and the loss at the start.
lessonObjectives.l5-stable-softmax: Write a softmax and a cross-entropy from logits that never overflow, and say why aloud.
lessonObjectives.l6-attention-from-scratch: Write causal multi-head attention in NumPy inside fifteen minutes, with the shapes checked.
lessonObjectives.l7-k-means-against-the-clock: Write k-means with a fixed start, an empty-cluster rule and a stopping test inside fifteen minutes.
lessonObjectives.l8-a-layers-backward-pass: Write the backward pass of a linear layer and a ReLU, checked by central differences.
lessonObjectives.l9-net-or-boosting: Frame the question of a network against boosting on tabular returns, and say what the evidence suggests.
lessonObjectives.l10-a-fair-comparison: Compare a network and boosting with the same splits, tuning budget and a paired test across days.
lessonObjectives.l11-when-the-net-wins: Build a simulated panel where a network beats boosting, and name the data shapes that cause it.
lessonObjectives.l12-the-case-aloud: Work the whole case aloud and answer the interviewer's follow-ups with numbers.
